screens.prompt: Put the average of the two highest times into C2, taking the values from the unsorted column.

hints.syntax: Two LARGE calls and a division: =(LARGE(B2:B6,1)+LARGE(B2:B6,2))/2.
hints.func-large: LARGE returns one position at a time, so ask it twice and average the pair.
hints.require-ref: Both calls point at B2:B6, so no time is typed into the formula.
hints.value: The two largest are 61 and 58. Add them, divide by two, and the cell holds 59.5.
hints.error: #NUM! comes from a position larger than the list, so check the 1 and the 2 in the two LARGE calls.

reject.why: the average of all five, 56.2, which includes the slow times
only the single best time, 61, so nothing has been averaged
Ben and Dev only, so the best two of the team are not in the range
the second best alone, 58, rather than the average of the pair
the second and third best, 57.5, which leaves the winner out
dividing by zero, so the cell holds #DIV/0!
the missing comma leaves LARGE with one unusable argument

screens.prompt: Put the place the middle time earns into C2, so the row shows where the median sits.

hints.func-median: The middle time is 57, a value in the list rather than a place in it.
hints.func-rank: Once MEDIAN returns 57, RANK turns that 57 into third place.
hints.require-ref: Both functions read B2:B6, so the comparison stays inside the team.
hints.value: The five times run 50, 55, 57, 58, 61, so 57 is third from the top.
hints.error: #N/A is the one to expect here: RANK looks for its number in the range, and a mean built from part of the list is not there.

reject.why: the middle time itself, 57, rather than the place it earns
the mean, 56.2, which is not a time in the list and has no place
Ada's own place, 2 — nothing has been asked about the middle of the list
division by zero, so the cell holds #DIV/0!
the closing bracket is missing, so nothing runs
the range leaves out B2, so the median is of four swimmers rather than five
twice the place, 6, which is outside a list of five

docs.explain:
A summary often needs two functions joined together, and Excel has none that averages the top two values on its own. The formula =(LARGE(B2:B6,1)+LARGE(B2:B6,2))/2 asks LARGE twice and divides by two. Read it inside out: each LARGE finds one value, the plus joins them, and the division finishes the job.

The five times are 58, 61, 55, 57 and 50, so LARGE picks 61 first and 58 second, and their average is 59.5. The second screen nests MEDIAN inside RANK: the middle time is 57, and 57 sits third from the top, so the answer is a place and not a time.

A mean of a subset can land on a number that appears nowhere in the data, so it has no row to inherit a format from. Two LARGE calls pointing at different ranges average two different groups, and nothing on the sheet says so.

errors.text: One of the LARGE positions runs past the end of the range, so there is no value to add.
RANK was given a number that is not in the range, which an average of a subset always produces: 59.5 appears nowhere among the times.
An argument in the nest arrived as text that cannot be read as a number.

docs.atWork: A selection report that averages a team's top two results, and a review sheet that shows where the median case sits in the ranked list.
docs.outcome: Join two summary functions into one answer, reading the nesting inside-out.
docs.dataset: One team's swim times summarised two ways

seo.title: Combine Excel summary functions
seo.description: LARGE asked twice and halved gives the average of the best two times. Nest MEDIAN inside RANK and the answer is a place. Read the trace inside-out.
